official.deadline_central_display: Early Decision I and Early Action: November 1; Early Decision II and Regular Decision: February 1 (annual decision-plan deadlines)
official.deadline_note: International first-year applicants follow the same decision plans and deadlines as other first-year applicants: Early Decision I and Early Action are due November 1, and Early Decision II and Regular Decision February 1. All financial aid materials must be submitted by the published application deadline for the chosen plan; the EducationUSA listing recorded 'Scholarship deadline same as application deadline: February 1, 2026' for the previous cycle.
official.application_cycle: Annual admission cycle (Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II, Regular Decision plans)
official.status_note: Trinity's international pages publish the standing annual decision-plan deadlines and describe merit scholarship consideration as automatic at admission, so the aid process runs with every admission round rather than as a separate competition.
official.tuition_coverage_note: International students are automatically considered for academic merit scholarships ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 per year, renewable for four years, or eight semesters.
benefits: Automatic consideration for general merit-based scholarships, historically ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 per year, with no separate application
Merit scholarships renewable for four years, or eight semesters
Need-based financial aid, described by EducationUSA as up to the cost of attendance, for applicants who demonstrate need
All international scholarships and financial aid are grants - Trinity does not offer loans to international students
Eligibility for Trinity on-campus employment for all international students regardless of financial need
eligibility: Applies for admission to Trinity University as an international undergraduate applicant (not a U.S. citizen or U.S. permanent resident), entering first-year or transfer
Submits the Statement of Financial Responsibility form in the Trinity admissions portal - the application cannot be reviewed until it is complete
For need-based aid: submits the CSS Profile for International Students or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application with the admission application

Merit scholarships are assessed on the rigour of and performance in secondary school coursework, standardized test scores, the strength of the essay, involvement outside the classroom, and recommendations from school officials
International transfer students are not eligible for Trinity financial aid
requirements: Submit the Common Application or the Coalition Application (no application fee for online applications)
Submit official secondary school records or transcripts in English, sent by a school counselor or school official - student-submitted records are not accepted
Submit proof of English language proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test) unless a waiver applies
Complete the Statement of Financial Responsibility in the Trinity admissions portal

For need-based aid, submit either the CSS Profile for International Students (Trinity code 6831) or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application, completed in English using USD for all calculations

CSS Profile for International Students (Trinity CSS code 6831) or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application (need-based aid only)

coverage: Academic merit scholarships historically ranging from $5,000 to $35,000 per year, renewable for four years or eight semesters
Need-based financial aid - up to the cost of attendance per the EducationUSA listing - for admitted international students who demonstrate need

application_method: Submit the admission application (Common App or Coalition App) under the chosen decision plan - there is no separate scholarship application
Complete the Statement of Financial Responsibility in the Trinity admissions portal; the application is not reviewed without it
If seeking need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile for International Students or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application with the admission application
Submit all financial aid materials by the published deadline for the chosen admission round
official.application_route: One admission application under a decision plan, with the Statement of Financial Responsibility in the portal; merit scholarship consideration is automatic and need-based aid rides on the same application.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants who are not U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents apply as international students regardless of where they attended secondary school; students in the process of applying for U.S. permanent residency also apply as international students
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are eligible for merit scholarships and need-based financial aid, though need-based funding is described as limited and competitive
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any of Trinity's undergraduate programmes (110+ areas of study); as an NCAA Division III school Trinity does not offer athletic scholarships, and student athletes are eligible for merit and need-based aid based on the admission application
official.duration: Merit scholarships are renewable for four years, or eight semesters
official.description: Trinity University offers international undergraduate students automatic consideration for merit-based scholarships - historically $5,000 to $35,000 per year and renewable for four years - plus limited, competitive need-based financial aid reviewed through a need-aware admissions process. All aid for international students is grant aid; the university does not offer loans to international students.
official.program_type: University-awarded merit scholarships plus competitive need-based grant aid for international undergraduates
official.english_requirement: Trinity requires proof of English language proficiency for all international applicants via TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo English Test. The international applicant guide publishes recommended scores (TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo - the TOEFL figure as currently published on the page appears inconsistent with the TOEFL score scale and should be confirmed with Admissions). Waivers are available where English is the applicant's first language and the primary language of the home or home country, or where English was the language of instruction for the final four consecutive years of secondary school (students in English language support courses in those four years are not eligible for a waiver).

applicant_utility.summary: At Trinity there is no separate scholarship application: your admission file is your scholarship file, so essay strength, coursework rigour and recommendations move the merit number directly, and the one form that genuinely gates everything is the Statement of Financial Responsibility - without it your application is not even reviewed. If you want need-based aid you must decide before you submit, because Trinity is need-aware and tells you that applying for aid puts you in its most competitive pool, with applicants contributing at least $45,000 per year the most competitive for admission. Deadlines are the standing decision-plan dates - November 1 for Early Decision I and Early Action, February 1 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision - and aid materials are due with the matching round, not later.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International first-year applicants with strong secondary school records who can either self-fund a meaningful share of costs or commit to the need-aware aid route early, and who are applying straight from secondary school rather than as transfers.
application_readiness_checklist: Complete the Statement of Financial Responsibility in the Trinity admissions portal as soon as the portal opens - the application cannot be reviewed without it
Decide before submitting whether you are applying for need-based aid, since the decision affects which admissions pool you are in
If seeking need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile (code 6831) or the Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application with the admission application, completed in English using USD
Have your school counselor or school official send official English transcripts directly - student-submitted records are not accepted
Book TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo early, and apply for an English-proficiency waiver only if you meet the four-year English-instruction criterion
Match your aid materials to your chosen decision plan's deadline (November 1 for ED I/EA, February 1 for ED II/RD)
common_rejection_risks: Leaving the Statement of Financial Responsibility incomplete, which stops the whole application from being reviewed
Submitting need-based aid materials after the decision-plan deadline - incomplete applications are not reviewed
Applying as an international transfer student expecting aid - Trinity states international transfer students are not eligible for Trinity financial aid
Expecting a loan package: Trinity offers no loans to international students, so your aid is grant-only
Applying as an athlete expecting a sports scholarship - as an NCAA Division III school Trinity offers none
Underestimating the need-aware trade-off: requesting need-based aid places you in the most competitive applicant pool
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Merit scholarships top out historically at $35,000 per year, and the EducationUSA listing frames need-based aid as up to the cost of attendance - so depending on award and need, tuition, fees, housing, food, insurance and flights can remain a substantial personal cost.
document_audit: Transcripts must arrive from the school counselor or school official, in English, and student-uploaded copies are not accepted as official
The CSS Profile must be submitted officially through College Board - screenshots are not accepted - and Trinity does not offer CSS Profile fee waivers, so budget for the fee
The Trinity International Student Financial Aid Application is the free alternative and must be completed in full, in English, using USD for all calculations
Duolingo results must come directly from the testing service; TOEFL and IELTS can be self-reported, but superscoring and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted
alerts: Merit scholarships renew for four years or eight semesters - check the renewal conditions in your award letter rather than assuming automatic renewal
Need-based aid must be re-applied for annually, and Satisfactory Academic Progress and full-time enrolment are conditions of keeping it
On-campus jobs are open to all international students but are not guaranteed - they supplement, not replace, the aid package
Watch the standing annual cycle: since aid is tied to admission rounds, missing the February 1 Regular Decision date pushes everything to the next year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One Common App or Coalition application under a decision plan, the Statement of Financial Responsibility in the portal, and optional need-based aid forms filed by the same deadline; merit outcomes arrive with the admission decision.
